title: Excel: Plan Mode lets Copilot outline a step-by-step plan before it changes a workbook
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing, user-selected default and governance controls are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The registry setting flagged by the pre-check is documented, and the briefing accurately reports the differing licensing descriptions without treating either as a Plan Mode-specific requirement.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet have a dedicated page for Plan Mode itself.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; controls[3].api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: No tenant or group control is documented for turning Plan Mode on or off separately from Copilot in Excel.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "Plan Mode" admin policy disable; "Excel" "plan mode" "admin"; Excel Plan Mode admin disable settings licensing meter documentation. Read Excel FAQ and copilotPolicySetting; no separate Plan Mode UI or API found.

claims.claim: Copilot in Excel is a Microsoft Copilot Chat tool and all Copilot Chat access settings apply.
claims.quote: Copilot in Excel is a Microsoft Copilot Chat tool and can't be turned off independently. All admin settings for controlling access to Microsoft Copilot Chat apply.

claims.claim: Group Policy Management exposes the analyze-content policy under User Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Office 2016 > Privacy > Trust Center.
claims.quote: If you’re using the Group Policy Management tool, all these policy settings are located under User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Office 2016\Privacy\Trust Center.

claims.claim: The policy label is Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content.
claims.quote: You can use the Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content policy setting to control whether these types of connected experiences are available to your users.

claims.claim: UserContentDisabled set to 2 disables the analyze-content policy under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy.
claims.quote:
| Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled  2=Disabled |
[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy]

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyze content removes Copilot features from Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word, including the Excel experience containing Plan Mode.
claims.quote:
If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:
- Excel
- OneNote
- Outlook
- PowerPoint
- Word

claims.claim: The connected-experiences privacy policies can also be configured through Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: These policy settings can be implemented by using either Group Policy or Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: The displayed Group Policy and registry settings have user scope.
claims.quote: User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Office 2016\Privacy\Trust Center

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label GUID> -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"} configures the label's content-analysis exclusion.
claims.quote: Set-Label -Identity "8faca7b8-8d20-48a3-8ea2-0f96310a848e" -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"}

claims.claim: BlockContentAnalysisServices is not configurable in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Searched: BlockContentAnalysisServices sensitivity label Microsoft Purview portal configuration. Read sensitivity-labels-office-apps and returned creation guidance; the setting's page explicitly says this configuration isn't available in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The label setting is configured through PowerShell after connecting to Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: You must use the PowerShell advanced setting BlockContentAnalysisServices with the Set-Label or New-Label cmdlet after you've connected to Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Content carrying a label configured with BlockContentAnalysisServices is excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot in the named Office apps, including Excel.
claims.quote: Although content with the configured sensitivity label will be excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot in the named Office apps, the content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios.

claims.claim: That labeled content remains available to Copilot in other scenarios such as Teams and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: the content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios. For example, in Teams, and in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Audit > Search > Workloads > Copilot reaches the Copilot audit workload filter.
claims.quote: Select Solutions > Audit. ... In Search > Workloads, select AIApp and Copilot. Select Search.

claims.claim: The AppHost property can identify interactions performed in Excel.
claims.quote: Other application-specific values: Values like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, Stream, and others indicate that the interaction was performed within these applications

claims.claim: Audit searches require a role that can search audit logs, such as Audit Reader.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal with a role that can search audit logs, like Audit Reader. Other roles can also search the audit logs.
